title: Trust Funding Checklist
description: Track each asset as you move it into your living trust or point it to the trust, so the trust controls what it should.
intro: A trust only controls the assets it holds. After signing, each account and property is either retitled in the trustee's name or set to pass to the trust at death. Work through this list with your attorney and check off each item as it is done.

sections.heading: Real estate
items: Sign and record a new deed for your home into the trust
Sign and record deeds for rental or vacation property
Record deeds for out-of-state property in that state's county
Notify your homeowner's insurer and add the trust as an insured
Ask your lender whether any notice is needed

sections.heading: Bank and investment accounts
items: Retitle checking and savings accounts in the trustee's name, or add a payable-on-death to the trust
Retitle brokerage accounts in the trustee's name
Retitle certificates of deposit at renewal or with the bank's form
Update any automatic transfers that depend on account titles

sections.heading: Retirement accounts and insurance
items: Ask your attorney whether to name the trust as beneficiary of each retirement account
Do not retitle retirement accounts into the trust, since that can trigger tax
Update life insurance beneficiaries if the plan calls for the trust
Update annuity beneficiaries where appropriate

sections.heading: Business and other assets
items: Assign LLC or partnership interests to the trust, checking the operating agreement first
Transfer corporate stock certificates to the trust
Sign a general assignment of personal property to the trust
Decide how vehicles will pass, since some states offer transfer-on-death titles
Assign promissory notes owed to you to the trust

sections.heading: Wrap-up
items: Keep a list of every asset and its funding status
Store confirmations with your trust document
Title new assets in the trust's name when you acquire them
Review funding once a year
